newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's 1997 GDP seen at 3.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Israel's 1997 GDP seen at 3.0 percent.

text.p: Economists at Israel Discount Bank forecast that Israeli gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 will grow only by 3.0 percent and call for an easing of the central bank's monetary policy to avoid an economic recession.
The Treasury's 1997 GDP forecast is of 4.3 percent against a GDP growth forecast of 5.5 percent in 1996.
In an economic survey, economists at the bank said the slowdown in growth was due mainly to the low profitability of companies caused by the high shekel and by a rise in real wages.

The economists said that a 3.0 percent GDP growth in 1997 means that GDP per capita is expected to grow in 1997 by less than one percent, against a growth of about two percent in 1996 and an average GDP per capita growth of about four percent in 1994 and 1995.
The lower profitability of the companies also causes a slowdown in investments in the economy.
The economists forecast the government's budget deficit for 1996 will be 4.0 percent of the GDP, against a target of 2.5 percent.
They call for an additional two billion shekels cut to the 1997 budget, over the 4.9 billion shekels 1997 budget cut which was approved by the government in July.

The survey forecasts the consumer price index will rise in the coming 12 months by 10 to 11 percent. The rise will be influenced mainly by the expected depreciation of the shekel in the coming months, the economists said.

"Considering that the target inflation rate for 1997 will be similar to that of 1996 and considering the slowdown in the economic activity, there is place for a certain easing of monetary restraint. This easing should be expressed in the lowering of the (central bank's) key lending rate (to commercial banks) that would bring it to 4.5 percent in real terms against 5.5 percent today," the economists said.

"The easing of monetary restraint and a significant cut in public consumption will help attain a real depreciation and will allow an improvement of profitability in the export sector. Without a fast undertaking of these steps in economic policy, the fiscal and monetary, the economy may slip into recession," the economists said.
